summary: At 24.5 square miles but only about 8,200 residents, Oak Hills sprawls across the high desert north of Hesperia with a population density of just 337 people per square mile — meaning your nearest neighbor's house might be visible but comfortably distant, set against a landscape of Joshua trees, creosote scrub, and wide-open Mojave sky. This is unambiguously a bedroom community; employment centers in Victorville, Hesperia, and Apple Valley sit along the I-15 and Highway 18 corridors to the south, and anyone working in the Inland Empire or Los Angeles basin faces a serious commute down the Cajon Pass. The affordability math, however, is the draw: a median home value of $475,500 against a median household income of $98,424 yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.8 — tight but far more approachable than most of Southern California. Rent at $2,102 a month consumes roughly 26% of that median income, which lands in manageable territory. With annual daytime highs averaging 71°F and nearly 10.7 hours of sunshine daily, the climate runs warm and dry, meaning summers are genuinely hot and winters bring cold desert nights dipping to the low 40s or below. The tradeoff that defines Oak Hills is elemental: abundant space and relative affordability purchased with distance from almost everything else.
